guide.title: Rights of Medication Administration
guide.lead: Every dose passes the same checks: right patient, drug, dose, route and time – plus a reason to give it, an assessment before, a reassessment after, and a record. Read the label three times, say it aloud, and stop if anything doesn't fit.

steps.title: 3. Before giving
steps.text: Read it aloud to your partner (closed loop); check the patient and allergies.

sections.title: Check before you give
rows: SBP 90 mmHg or more; no sildenafil or vardenafil in 24 hours, no tadalafil in 48 hours; right-sided ECG in inferior STEMI
Concentration in mg/mL: 1 mg/mL is IM; 0.1 mg/mL is IV in arrest
notes: Ratio labels (1:1000, 1:10,000) are being replaced by mg/mL because they cause tenfold errors.

sections.title: After you give it
items: Reassess effect and side effects: vital signs, symptoms, SpO₂
Document drug, dose, route, time, who gave it, response – after giving, not before

quiz.q: Correct use of the three-check system for albuterol:
options: Check when taking it out, when preparing it, and before giving it
Once when you pick it up
quiz.explanation: Each check covers name, concentration, dose and expiry.

quiz.q: Chest pain, SBP 96, took sildenafil 12 hours ago. Nitroglycerin?
options: No: sildenafil within 24 hours contraindicates nitrates

quiz.q: A nurse hands you a pre-filled syringe 'for Mrs Johnson's seizures, give it IM'. You:
options: Confirm the patient with 2 identifiers, check she is seizing, verify drug, dose and route yourself
Give it while calling medical direction
quiz.explanation: You are responsible for every drug you give.

options: Reassess breath sounds, work of breathing, SpO₂ and heart rate

quiz.q: How many identifiers should confirm a patient's identity?
quiz.explanation: Name and date of birth, or ID band.

quiz.q: Glucagon should be given only after:
When do you document a drug?
options: At the end of the shift

quiz.q: A capable patient refuses aspirin. You:
options: Explain the risk, respect the decision and document it

quiz.q: Tadalafil was taken 30 hours ago. Nitroglycerin is:

flashcards.question: Five original rights
flashcards.answer: Right patient, drug, dose, route, time.

flashcards.question: Expanded rights
flashcards.answer: Right indication, right assessment before, right evaluation after, right documentation, right to refuse.

flashcards.question: Three-check system
flashcards.answer: When taking it out, when preparing it, immediately before giving it: name, concentration, dose, expiry. Read aloud.

flashcards.question: Identifying the patient
flashcards.answer: At least 2 identifiers: ID band, name and date of birth, or a carer's confirmation. Never a room number.

flashcards.question: Checks before common drugs
flashcards.answer: Nitroglycerin: SBP 90 mmHg or more, no PDE-5 inhibitor (24 hours sildenafil/vardenafil, 48 hours tadalafil). Albuterol: wheeze, HR, SpO₂. Glucagon/dextrose: glucose below 70 mg/dL.

flashcards.question: When to document
flashcards.answer: After giving: drug, dose, route, time, who gave it and the response.

flashcards.question: Informed refusal of a drug
flashcards.answer: Capacity, understanding of risks and benefits, documented with their reasons.

flashcards.question: Epinephrine concentrations
flashcards.answer: 1 mg/mL (old label 1:1000) for IM anaphylaxis. 0.1 mg/mL (old 1:10,000) for IV in arrest. Giving 1 mg/mL IV by mistake is a tenfold error.

critical.scenario: Nursing home, COPD flare. Your partner pulls out a nebule and starts to give it before you've identified the patient or listened to the chest.
critical.question: Most appropriate response?

options.t: Pause: confirm identity with 2 identifiers, check allergies, assess wheeze and vital signs, verify drug and dose aloud, then give and reassess

critical.explanation: A few seconds of checks prevents most errors.
critical.kpi: Applies the rights of medication administration under time pressure

critical.scenario: You plan fentanyl 50 mcg IV. Your partner hands you a 2 mL vial labelled 100 mcg/2 mL and you nearly draw up the whole vial.
critical.question: What does this near miss teach?

options.t: Read the concentration, not just the total: 100 mcg/2 mL is 50 mcg/mL, so 50 mcg is 1 mL. Read labels aloud and double-check calculations

options.f: Near misses should be reported and learned from.

critical.kpi: Verifies concentration and calculates volume correctly

critical.scenario: 60-year-old with typical chest pain, capable, refuses aspirin because 'it upsets my stomach'.
critical.question: Management?

options.t: Explain the benefit briefly, respect his refusal, document his capacity and reasons, continue other care

options.f: He refused one drug, not all care.

critical.explanation: Tell the hospital he hasn't had aspirin.
